questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by the car driver not giving the rider the right-of-way?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
Over 50 percent
About 90 percent

questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver did not give the rider the right-of-way.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of these should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk whenever they want.

questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and still to help you focus on riding. They should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, why should you not move to the far side of your lane?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
It encourages the passing driver to pass more quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut back too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane is dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding so other drivers can see you. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you accidentally lock the rear brake on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer the motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: To turn your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking pace, your motorcycle will lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: During the day, your headlight should:

options.text: Not be used.
Be on high beam.
Be on low beam.
Switch between high and low beam.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: If you brake while turning a curve:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction from leaning into the curve.
You may have less traction because you are leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction because you are leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. The tire grip is partly used for turning while leaning, so less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is slippery. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them with straps or in saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back of the seat raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Always distribute weight evenly on both sides.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the lead rider.
At the back of the group.
Anywhere within the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch over them from behind.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Always apply the brakes first, then swerve.
Try instead to use only the brakes.

questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving as separate actions. Do one first, then the other. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Try to move onto the shoulder.
Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far to the side may encourage the driver to return too early.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes fully to stop in a straight line without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: As your weight shifts to the front while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Not worry. The weight transfer will not have an effect on your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle's weight moves forward during braking, gradually increase pressure on the front brake lever.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front, just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them without making inexperienced riders lead.

questions.question: When a vehicle tries to pass you from behind, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
Not be concerned about which portion of the lane you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This reduces the risk of collision with the passing vehicle.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
You can see hazards in the next lane better.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see hazards in the next lane better.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. This position gives you a better view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Riders who wear helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, regardless of your speed.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket prevents dehydration and protects you, even in warm weather. Most jackets are designed to protect riders from overheating.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than you normally would.
Start slowing down earlier than you normally would.
Increase your following distance.
Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle will slow down and stop more slowly. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, and keep more distance behind other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.
